title: FACET: Multi-Agent AI Supporting Teachers in Scaling Differentiated Learning for Diverse Students
extended_summary:
This paper addresses how AI can support teachers in providing differentiated instruction in increasingly heterogeneous classrooms. The authors argue that most existing AI education tools are student-facing and adapt mainly to performance, while effective differentiation also requires attention to motivation, language proficiency, and learning differences such as dyslexia and ADHD. The study asks whether a teacher-facing multi-agent AI system can better fit classroom workflows and produce pedagogically appropriate materials for diverse learner profiles.

The paper introduces FACET, a teacher-in-the-loop multi-agent framework composed of four agents: a learner simulation agent, a diagnostic assessment agent, a material generation agent, and an evaluation agent. Teachers define learner profiles, upload or select tasks, and review generated outputs before use. The system is designed to generate curriculum-aligned, accessibility-aware worksheets, especially for mathematics, while preserving teacher control. Technically, the framework uses a local open-source large language model and a structured orchestration process to generate differentiated worksheets in about 30 seconds.

The empirical evaluation combines qualitative workshops with 30 German school principals and a quantitative online survey with 70 in-service K-12 teachers recruited via Prolific from the United Kingdom, United States, Canada, and Australia. The survey focused on grade 7 mathematics area-calculation worksheets representing different learner profiles, including motivation, performance, and dyslexia-related needs. Principals commented on practical relevance, teacher workload, curriculum alignment, accessibility, and the need to maintain pedagogical autonomy; teachers rated five example worksheets on didactic structure, clarity, format/design, creativity, and, for the dyslexia version, readability-related features.

The main conclusions are that FACET shows strong perceived value as a teacher-facing AI tool for inclusive differentiation, especially for scaffolded materials for struggling or low-motivation learners. Participants viewed teacher-in-the-loop control and curriculum alignment as essential for adoption. However, the study also found weaker ratings for enrichment materials for advanced learners and only moderate success for dyslexia-specific typography and readability. The authors conclude that FACET is promising for supporting differentiated instruction at scale, but that classroom deployment, validation against real student responses, and longitudinal evaluation are still needed.
study_country: Germany; United Kingdom; United States; Canada; Australia

identified_tools.name: FACET
identified_tools.description: A teacher-facing multi-agent AI framework for generating differentiated instructional materials using four coordinated agents for learner simulation, diagnostic assessment, material generation, and evaluation within a teacher-in-the-loop workflow.
identified_tools.use_case: Studied as a research framework to help K–12 teachers generate curriculum-aligned, differentiated grade-7 mathematics worksheets tailored to learner profiles including differences in motivation, performance, and dyslexia-related processing needs.

findings.finding_summary: In exploratory workshops, school principals reported strong perceived practical relevance of FACET for reducing teacher workload and supporting differentiated instruction in heterogeneous classrooms. Across two workshops with N=30 principals, participants emphasized the need for curriculum alignment, accessibility, configurable learner profiles, and teacher-in-the-loop control as prerequisites for adoption; no effect size was reported.
findings.measure: Qualitative workshop themes on practical relevance, usability, workflow integration, and adoption conditions

findings.finding_summary: In a survey of K–12 teachers evaluating FACET-generated grade-7 math worksheets, didactic structure and clarity were rated favorably for most learner profiles. Among N=70 teachers, worksheet ratings on a 6-point scale included didactic structure of M=4.50 (SD=1.02) and clarity M=4.46 (SD=1.05) for high-performance/low-motivation materials, and didactic structure M=4.41 (SD=1.06) and clarity M=4.23 (SD=1.16) for low-performance/low-motivation materials.
findings.measure: Teacher ratings of generated worksheet didactic structure and clarity on 6-point Likert scales

findings.finding_summary: FACET-generated enrichment materials for advanced learners were rated lower than scaffolded materials. For the high-performance, high-motivation worksheet evaluated by N=70 teachers, ratings were didactic structure M=3.87 (SD=1.17), clarity M=3.57 (SD=1.20), format M=3.10 (SD=1.37), and creativity M=3.30 (SD=1.34), suggesting the system currently supports scaffolded content better than enrichment-oriented materials.
findings.measure: Teacher ratings of enrichment worksheet quality across didactic structure, clarity, format/design, and creativity

findings.finding_summary: For the dyslexia-adapted worksheet, teachers judged some accessibility adaptations favorably but identified shortcomings in typography. Among N=70 teachers, spacing/layout was rated M=4.07 (SD=1.39) and language simplification M=3.94 (SD=1.40), while font readability was lower at M=3.30 (SD=1.61) and overall suitability for reading difficulties was M=3.46 (SD=1.47).
findings.measure: Teacher ratings of dyslexia-related accessibility features: suitability for reading difficulties, font readability, language simplification, and spacing/layout

quality_tier_rationale: This is an empirical mixed-methods evaluation of a specific named system, but outcomes are based on practitioner workshops and teacher ratings rather than student learning gains or a controlled experimental design.
impact_tier_rationale: Findings indicate promising perceived usefulness and generally favorable worksheet-quality ratings, but impact on student outcomes is unclear and no causal effect sizes are reported.
